tagline: Fine jewellery, made by hand in Kala Ghoda since 1978.
description: Aranya is a family jewellery atelier in Kala Ghoda, Mumbai: hallmarked gold, polki and precious stones, made to order and by appointment.

pages.title: Aranya — Fine jewellery in Kala Ghoda, Mumbai
pages.description: Hallmarked gold, polki and precious stones, made by hand in our Kala Ghoda atelier since 1978. View by appointment.

sections.headline: Heirlooms, *made slowly*
sections.lede: Every Aranya piece is drawn, set and polished by hand in our atelier above Rampart Row — then hallmarked, and made to be handed down.

sections.text: Jewellery should outlive the *occasion* it was made for. So we make fewer pieces, and we make them to last a hundred years.

items.title: It begins at the *bench*
items.text: Every piece starts as a pencil drawing, made with you if it is a commission. We draw until it feels inevitable.

$photo.q: Hands sketching jewellery designs at a desk
$photo.alt: Hands sketching jewellery designs at a desk

items.title: Chosen *in person*
items.text: We choose each stone ourselves and certify it independently. You see the certificate before we set it.

$photo.q: A round diamond beside a blue gemstone
$photo.alt: A round diamond beside a blue gemstone

items.title: The old way, *no shortcuts*
items.text: Our karigars solder, set and finish by hand — polki in pure gold foil, never glue.

$photo.q: An artisan soldering a piece of jewellery with a torch
$photo.alt: An artisan soldering a piece of jewellery with a torch

items.title: Hallmarked, and *polished for life*
items.text: Every gold piece carries the BIS hallmark, and comes back to us for free polishing whenever you like.

$photo.q: A jeweller polishing a gold ring
$photo.alt: A jeweller polishing a gold ring

sections.title: A private *viewing*
sections.text: Sit with us at the atelier, try pieces on in natural light, and talk through a commission. There is no charge and no obligation.

items.a: Yes. Every gold piece carries the BIS hallmark and a unique HUID number you can verify on the BIS Care app.

items.q: Can you remake my grandmother's jewellery?
items.a: Often, yes. Bring it to a viewing; we will tell you honestly what can be kept, reset or melted, and give you a written estimate.

items.q: How long does a commission take?
items.a: Usually five to eight weeks, depending on the stones. We send photographs at each stage.
Yes, fully insured, anywhere in India. Or collect from the atelier.
